settings.chronicleFrequency_tooltip: How often the court historian writes a chronicle entry. Disabled turns off automatic generation.
settings.chronicleRawSourceCharLimit_tooltip: Maximum total characters of raw source material sent to the model. Sources exceeding this limit are summarized.
settings.chronicleOutputMaxTokens_tooltip: Maximum tokens for the generated chronicle entry.
settings.max_tokens_tooltip: The maximum number of tokens (words/characters) the AI can generate in a single response. Higher values allow for longer replies.
settings.max_memory_tokens_tooltip: The maximum number of tokens to use for character memories. This affects how much of their past experiences the AI can recall.
settings.clean_tooltip: The mod will try to remove parts of the messages that the llm shouldn't have generated, like emojis
settings.shuffle_tooltip: Randomize the order in which characters generate messages in multi-character conversations. Note: If enabled, the speaking order of each character will be random, which may lead to confusion in the LLM's output character identity.
settings.dynamic_tooltip: Use LLM to analyze conversation and select the next character to speak. The LLM will choose from a pool of characters who haven't spoken yet in the current round.
settings.nonTargetedCharacterResponseChance_toolt: The chance (0-100%) that a non-targeted character will respond in a multi-character conversation after the targeted character has spoken.
settings.questionPlayerActionsChance_tooltip: The chance (0-100%) that an AI character will question the player's actions based on their personality and the situation.
settings.validate_tooltip: When streaming is disabled and there are more than 2 characters, validate that the generated message matches the character's identity. If validation fails, regenerate up to 3 times.
settings.show_suggestions_tooltip: Show or hide the suggestions button in the chat window. Controls whether to display the recommended input statements feature.
settings.disable_historical_tooltip: Disable loading of historical conversations that prepopulate the chat window with previous conversations with that character.
settings.max_historical_conversations_tooltip: The maximum number of historical conversation files to load. Helps prevent lag with characters that have a long history. Set to 0 for no limit.
settings.max_conversations_in_history_window_tool: The maximum number of previous conversations to display in the chat window. This does not affect the AI's memory, only what you see.
settings.generate_scene_tooltip: Generate scene description at the start of conversation to provide context and background for characters.
settings.auto_suggestions_tooltip: When enabled, suggestions will be automatically generated at the start of conversation and after each round of dialogue.
settings.auto_send_tooltip: When enabled, selecting a suggestion will automatically send the message without clicking the send button.
settings.show_tokenizer_tooltip: When enabled, shows a real-time token count display in the chat window.
settings.manual_approval_tooltip: If enabled, actions triggered by the AI must be manually approved by the user in the chat window before they are executed.
settings.max_summaries_tooltip: The maximum number of summaries (conversation, letter, diary) to include in the prompt. Helps control token count.
settings.ai_start_tooltip: Allows the AI to initiate the conversation. The chance is determined by the percentage field below.
settings.aiToAiChatChance_tooltip: The chance that an AI character, after responding to the player, will also send a message to another AI character.
settings.maxConsecutiveActions_tooltip: The maximum number of consecutive AI responses that can trigger actions. Helps prevent action loops. Set to 0 for no limit.
settings.diary_chance_tooltip: The chance (0-100%) that a diary entry will be generated for a character after a conversation. An entry is always generated if the character was involved in an action.
settings.stream_tooltip: Receive the AI's response as it's being generated, word by word. Disabling this may result in longer wait times but can be more compatible with some models.
settings.summaries_depth_tooltip: How many messages from the end of the conversation to insert the summary of past conversations. 0 means at the very beginning.
settings.memories_depth_tooltip: How many messages from the end of the conversation to insert character memories. 0 means at the very beginning.
settings.desc_depth_tooltip: How many messages from the end of the conversation to insert the character description. 0 means at the very beginning.
settings.memory_compaction_desc: Automatically compresses conversation history to save context space while preserving key narrative details.
settings.memory_compaction_enable_tooltip: Turn on automatic compaction of old conversations
settings.phase1_threshold_desc: Percentage of context window to trigger Phase 1 compaction
settings.phase1_threshold_tooltip: When token usage exceeds this percentage, Phase 1 compaction will run
settings.phase2_threshold_desc: Number of Phase 1 summaries before triggering Phase 2
settings.phase2_threshold_tooltip: When this many Phase-1 summaries exist, Phase 2 compaction will consolidate them
settings.token_budget_tooltip: How context tokens are split between Phase 1 and Phase 2 compaction
settings.phase1_budget_desc: Percentage of context allocated to Phase 1 summaries
settings.phase2_budget_desc: Percentage of context allocated to Phase 2 summaries

settings.priority_elements_desc: Narrative elements to preserve during compaction

settings.compaction_context_usage_tooltip: Live view of how much of the AI context window is currently in use. Approaches the Phase 1 threshold line as conversation grows.
settings.quick_model_connection_desc: Optional low-latency LLM for quick decisions (character targeting, etc.). Uses the text generation connection by default.
settings.quick_model_use_text_gen_tooltip: When enabled, the Quick Model will share the text generation API connection.

settings.cleartargetaftersend_tooltip: Automatically clear the target character dropdown after sending a message

settings.cleanMessages_tooltip: The mod will try to remove parts of messages that the LLM should not have generated, such as emojis.
settings.shuffleCharacterOrder_tooltip: Randomize the order in which characters generate messages in multi-character conversations. This may confuse character identity in LLM output.

readme.subtitle: AI conversation mod for Crusader Kings III
readme.step1_1: Click on the 'Connection' option in the left menu
readme.step1_2: Select your text generation API provider (e.g., OpenAI, Kobold, etc.)
readme.step1_3: Enter your API key and related configurations
readme.step1_4: Set the CK3 user folder path (usually located in 'Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III')
readme.step2_3: Right-click on any character in the game
readme.step3_desc: When you initiate a conversation in the game, Voices of the Court will automatically pop up a chat window where you can:
readme.step3_2: Influence game state and character relationships
readme.step3_3: Experience dynamically generated character personality traits
readme.warning_desc: Before first use, please ensure that the Voices of the Court 2.0 - Community Edition mod is enabled in the game and correctly installed according to the mod instructions.
readme.feat1_desc: Engage in intelligent dialogue with any character in the game. The AI generates appropriate responses based on the character's personality, traits, and current context.
readme.feat2_desc: The AI dynamically generates unique personality traits and dialogue styles based on the character's traits, skills, and relationships.
readme.feat3_desc: Automatically generate summaries for long conversations to maintain context and avoid token limit issues.
readme.feat4_desc: Detect various actions in the game (such as opinion changes, giving money, etc.) and generate corresponding AI narratives.
readme.feat5_desc: Import specific playbooks to fill the game world view and character summaries.
readme.adv_feat1: Multi-character Dialogue: Support for conversing with multiple characters simultaneously
readme.adv_feat2: Character Validation: Ensure AI-generated responses match character identity
readme.adv_feat3: Dynamic Character Selection: AI intelligently selects the next character to respond
readme.adv_feat4: Custom Prompts: Fully customize AI behavior and response styles
readme.adv_feat5: Conversation History Management: View and manage all conversation records
readme.conf_conn_desc: Configure the connection with the language model API and game path settings.
readme.conf_conn_api1: API Provider: Select text generation API (OpenAI, KoboldAI, Text Generation WebUI, OobaBooga, Player2, etc.)
readme.conf_conn_api2: API Key: Enter the API key for the selected service
readme.conf_conn_api3: Endpoint URL: The URL address of the API service
readme.conf_conn_api4: Model Name: Select the specific model to use
readme.conf_conn_path1: Path Setting: Set the CK3 folder path where user data is stored
readme.conf_conn_path2: Default Path: Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III
readme.conf_conn_path3: Selection Method: Browse and select the correct path via the 'Select Folder' button
readme.conf_act_desc: Configure detectable actions in the game and corresponding AI responses.
readme.conf_act_enable1: Master Switch: Controls whether to enable the action detection feature
readme.conf_act_enable2: Enable AI Narrative: Generate AI narrative descriptions after actions are triggered
readme.conf_act_api1: Same Settings: Use the same API configuration as the Connection page
readme.conf_act_api2: Independent Configuration: Configure API settings separately for the action feature
readme.conf_act_param1: Temperature: Controls the creativity of AI responses (default 0.2, lower values make responses more deterministic)
readme.conf_act_param2: Frequency Penalty: Reduces the generation of repetitive content
readme.conf_act_param3: Presence Penalty: Encourages talking about new topics
readme.conf_act_param4: Top P: Controls the diversity of vocabulary selection
readme.conf_act_sel1: Action List: Select the types of actions you want the mod to detect from the list
readme.conf_act_sel2: Action Info: Each action has a description and creator information
readme.conf_act_sel3: Reload Files: Button to refresh the action list
readme.conf_act_sel4: Open Folder: Button to access custom action scripts
readme.conf_sum_desc: Configure API settings for the conversation summary feature.
readme.conf_sum_api1: Same Settings: Use the same API configuration as the Connection page

step1.title: Welcome to the Prompt Workbench
step1.body1: VOTC can capture real in-game conversations (campaign and legacy-player scopes) so you can replay them here, edit prompt variants and compare outputs.
step1.body2: Captured samples are stored inside the app data folder (votc_data/prompt_workbench).
step1.body3: Captured content is sensitive: it contains in-game secrets and private conversations. Retention is rolling (default 30 per scope, up to 200) and a per-scope quota (default 100 MB) bounds disk usage.

step2.title: Capture setting
step2.bodyOff: Capture is currently OFF. It is opt-in: open the app config window (system tray → Open config window → Prompt workbench) and enable it there. The wizard never turns capture on for you.
step2.bodyOn: Capture is ON. New in-game conversations will appear as samples in the library below.
step2.settingsHint: Retention count and quota are also configured in the app config window.

step3.title: Play one real conversation
step3.body1: Close this window, play CK3 with the VOTC mod and finish a real conversation (a few turns). Come back here - the captured conversation will be in the Sample library.

step4.title: Your first sample
step4.ready: Samples are here. Open one in the Sample library, then press “New variant” in the variant editor to copy the Production prompt into an editable variant (frozen input) — the captured literal baseline stays untouched for comparison.
step4.waiting: No samples yet. After a real in-game conversation with capture enabled, the captured sample appears here automatically.

step5.title: Edit one low-risk field
step5.body1: In the variant editor, change ONE low-risk field first (for example a suffix sentence). Keep everything else inherited - a small first change makes the comparison readable.

step6.title: Check the diff and the tokens
step6.body1: Open the Diff tab: it compares your variant against the captured literal baseline line by line. The preview also shows the estimated input tokens, so you can see the cost impact of your edit.

step7.title: Connection and cost
step7.body1: Below are the connection identities, request count and token estimates for the planned experiment. Review them, then acknowledge the cost to continue.
step7.acknowledge: I understand this will send real API requests and incur real costs.

step8.title: Run one two-variant experiment
step8.body1: Create an experiment with the literal baseline plus your edited variant and run it. Stop only cancels queued requests - an in-flight request finishes and keeps its result.

step9.title: Score and export
step9.body1: Rate the outputs blindly (variant names stay hidden until every run is rated), read the conclusion and export the report as Markdown. You are done - the workbench is yours.
